segment_1.topic_phrase: who actually has the right of way when somebody is crossing the road
segment_1.setup: I'm **{{INTERVIEWER}}**, and today we're talking about crosswalks. There's one thing almost everybody in Florida gets wrong about them, and it matters a great deal if you ever get hit.
segment_1.credential: **{{ATTORNEY}}**, after **{{YEARS_PRACTICING}}** years in these courts you know how the local insurers are going to argue a case like this before they say a word.
segment_1.prompt: There's one thing people around here get wrong about crosswalks more than anything else. Set us straight. And if you've seen it cost somebody their case, tell us about that one.

attributes.name: Tried a failure to yield
attributes.detail: Cases you took to a jury, and what they did with a driver who simply didn't give way.

attributes.name: People struck crossing
attributes.detail: Not injury cases generally. People hit while on foot, how many, and how recently.

attributes.name: Your record beats a rating
attributes.detail: Your license and your disciplinary history are public, and anyone can look them up. A review score isn't.

attributes.name: How a jury here hears it
attributes.detail: The county court, the judges, and what a local jury assumes about somebody who was walking.

attributes.name: Knowing the crossings
attributes.detail: The corridors and intersections where this keeps happening, and what's actually wrong with them.

attributes.name: Storefront footage
attributes.detail: What you secure in the first days, because video from a shop facing the crossing is gone inside a month.

attributes.name: Reading the road
attributes.detail: Crash reconstruction experts, the treating doctors, and engineers who can explain what was wrong with the crossing itself.

attributes.name: Coverage with no car
attributes.detail: How somebody who doesn't own a vehicle may still have coverage, and which policy pays first.

attributes.name: The two deadlines
attributes.detail: The two-week medical window and the filing deadline, said as numbers, and what each one costs if it passes.

attributes.name: Your fee and the costs
attributes.detail: The percentage, whether it rises if you file suit, who pays to get the footage and the road data, and what happens if you lose.

attributes.name: Who they reach at night
attributes.detail: Whether the client is hiring you or an intake operation, and who picks up at nine in the evening.

attributes.name: When the person was in the wrong
attributes.detail: The cases where somebody genuinely wasn't crossing lawfully, and why you say that up front rather than at the end.

questions.q: Who actually has the right of way at a crosswalk in Stuart?

bullets.label: The person walking, once they're in it
bullets.detail: traffic has to yield to you, and the one exception is stepping out in front of a car that's already too close to stop.

bullets.label: The paint isn't what makes it a crosswalk
bullets.detail: the duty to yield applies at corners that were never painted, and that's where most of the fighting happens.

bullets.label: Where it matters most here
bullets.detail: US 1 through downtown, where the shops and restaurants are on both sides and the marked crossings are a long way apart.

questions.q: What does the law actually require a driver to do at a marked crosswalk?

bullets.label: Yield, not creep
bullets.detail: a driver has to give way to somebody already in a marked crossing, and on a multilane road the drivers in the other lanes have to stop too, rather than swinging around the car that stopped.

bullets.label: Speed is part of it
bullets.detail: a driver who can't stop for somebody already crossing was going too fast for that crossing.

bullets.label: Stopping means stopping
bullets.detail: if you roll through while somebody is still in the road you've already broken the rule, and it doesn't have to be a close call.

questions.q: Do you still have any rights crossing outside a crosswalk in Florida?

bullets.label: You do, but you've to yield
bullets.detail: away from a crossing the traffic has the right of way, not you.

bullets.label: That doesn't make you fair game
bullets.detail: a driver who sees you and doesn't slow down is still responsible for hitting you.

bullets.label: Florida never legalized jaywalking
bullets.detail: if you're between two intersections that both have signals, you're supposed to use a marked crosswalk, whatever people assume.

questions.q: How is it decided who was right at an intersection in Stuart with no painted crossing?

bullets.label: An unpainted crossing is still a crossing
bullets.detail: at a downtown corner on US 1 with no paint at all, the crossing is legally there and the duty to yield comes with it.

bullets.label: It's where the sidewalk would continue
bullets.detail: the crossing legally exists along the line the sidewalk takes across the road.

bullets.label: Nobody knows this
bullets.detail: which is why the driver, the insurer and sometimes the officer all get it wrong at the scene.

questions.q: How does a car that's turning or backing up end up hitting someone?

bullets.label: They're looking the other way
bullets.detail: a driver turning right is watching for a gap in traffic, not for a person already in the crossing.

bullets.label: A driver backing up can barely see
bullets.detail: in a lot of vehicles there's a stretch right behind the bumper you can't see at all without a camera.

bullets.label: The walk signal doesn't stop them
bullets.detail: having the signal means you were lawfully there, not that the car saw you.

questions.q: What proves somebody was crossing lawfully in Stuart?

bullets.label: Where they were standing
bullets.detail: the point of impact relative to the crossing settles most of the argument by itself.

bullets.label: What was recording
bullets.detail: the shops, restaurants and banks along US 1 and Kanner Highway keep their own cameras, and a lot of that footage is gone inside a month.

bullets.label: Who saw it
bullets.detail: whoever was waiting at the same corner, and anyone working at a business facing the crossing.

questions.q: How does failing to yield actually establish that a driver was at fault?

bullets.label: There's a rule they broke
bullets.detail: the duty to yield to somebody in a crossing is written into the law, so we'ren't arguing about whether the driver was careful enough.

bullets.label: It changes what we argue about
bullets.detail: we're no longer arguing whether the driver was careful, we're arguing what this cost you.

bullets.label: Nobody has to get a ticket
bullets.detail: a driver who was never cited still broke the same rule.

questions.q: What happens if the person walking was partly in the wrong?

bullets.label: It reduces what you get, it doesn't wipe it out
bullets.detail: your share of the fault comes off the recovery, and being partly wrong doesn't end the case.

bullets.label: But there's a hard line
bullets.detail: in Florida, if you're found more than fifty percent at fault, you recover nothing at all.

bullets.label: It's the whole fight
bullets.detail: the insurer will say you crossed somewhere other than a marked crosswalk, and on a road where the crossings are half a mile apart that's easy for them to say and very beatable.

questions.q: How do distracted and speeding drivers cause these crashes in Stuart and across the Treasure Coast?

bullets.label: They're looking down
bullets.detail: a driver checking a phone at a green light has no idea anybody stepped off the curb.

bullets.label: Speed removes the option
bullets.detail: a few miles an hour is the difference between a hard stop and no stop at all.

bullets.label: Where it concentrates here
bullets.detail: US 1 and Kanner Highway, where the road is built for speed and people are still crossing it on foot to get between businesses.

questions.q: What injuries actually happen when a car hits a person?

bullets.label: There'sn'thing protecting you
bullets.detail: the head, the pelvis and the legs take the force, and even a low-speed impact does serious damage.

bullets.label: Two impacts, not one
bullets.detail: the vehicle, and then the road, and the second one is often the worse of the two.

bullets.label: Where people get treated here
bullets.detail: Cleveland Clinic Martin North handles the emergency room side, and the most serious injuries get moved out of the county to the trauma center in Fort Pierce.
